title: Base change for the dualizing object of a projection
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension
$d$, put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta=(\operatorname{id}_X,\operatorname{id}_X):X\to W$. The square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
W& \xrightarrow{\ p_2\ }&X\\
p_1\big\downarrow &&\big\downarrow f\\
X&\xrightarrow{\ f\ }&Y
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian and $p_1$ is smooth (the base change of $f$); by the
base-change theorem [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] (the comparison of
[def-pur-co-smoothness]),

$$
\omega_{p_1}=Rp_1^!\Lambda_X
\;\cong\;Lp_2^*Rf^!\Lambda_Y=Lp_2^*\omega_f,
$$

and symmetrically $\omega_{p_2}\cong Lp_1^*\omega_f$. Here $C$ denotes the section invariant of [def-pur-section-invariant]. In
particular, since $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$,

$$
C(p_1,\Delta)=L\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}
\;\cong\;L\Delta^*Lp_2^*\omega_f
\;\cong\;\omega_f.
$$

proof.text: By [def-pc-fibre-product], $W=X\times_YX$ has $fp_1=fp_2$ and represents pairs of maps into $X$ having equal composites with $f$. Thus the displayed square is Cartesian. The pair $(\operatorname{id}_X,\operatorname{id}_X)$ defines $\Delta$ and gives both $p_1\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$ and $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$. Separatedness of $f$ says exactly that this diagonal is a closed immersion, by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The first projection is the base change of $f$ along $f$ with the roles of the two copies of $X$ labelled as in the displayed square; for the second projection, the square with upper map $p_1$ and left map $p_2$ is Cartesian because compatible maps $a:T\to X$ to the lower copy and $b:T\to X$ to the right copy uniquely lift as $(b,a):T\to W$. Thus $p_2$ is also a base change of $f$ along $f$. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] (1) to get smoothness of relative dimension $d$ for both projections. They are separated and of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to the separated finite-type morphism $f$ of the fixed purity setting: [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] specifies that $X,Y$ are finite-type schemes over the fixed field and $f$ is a separated finite-type morphism. For completeness, $W$ is also a finite-type scheme over the fixed field: by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with each $B_i$ finitely generated over the field, then a finite affine cover of each $p_1^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}B_i)$ by $\operatorname{Spec}C_{ij}$ with $C_{ij}$ finitely generated over $B_i$. The union of generators of $B_i$ over the field and of $C_{ij}$ over $B_i$ generates $C_{ij}$ over the field; these finitely many affine opens cover $W$. In particular $(p_1,\Delta)$ meets the geometric hypotheses of the section-invariant definition.

proof.text: Apply the base-change clause of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] to $X'=W$, $Y'=X$, $u=p_2$, $v=f$, and $f'=p_1$. Its hypothesis is that the original vertical map $f$ is smooth separated of relative dimension $d$, which is assumed. Its base map $v$ is arbitrary, so this application is permitted even though $f$ need not be proper or etale. The theorem gives the canonical isomorphism $b_1:Lp_2^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_1}$. Taking $b_1^{-1}$ gives precisely $\omega_{p_1}\cong Lp_2^*\omega_f$, with $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ and $\omega_{p_1}=Rp_1^!\Lambda_X$.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: specialize base change to $Y\prime=X$, $g=f$, $g\prime=p_2$, $f\prime=p_1$; supplied by sk-prop-cohsm clause (c)

proof.text: Use the Cartesian square established in Step 1 with upper map $p_1$ and left map $p_2$: take $X'=W$, $Y'=X$, $u=p_1$, $v=f$, $f'=p_2$. The original vertical map is the assumed smooth separated $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$, and the lower base map is $f:X\to Y$; arbitrary base maps are allowed. Step 1 supplies the required finite-type schemes and morphisms. The base-change clause of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] now gives $b_2:Lp_1^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_2}$. Its inverse is the claimed symmetric comparison $\omega_{p_2}\cong Lp_1^*\omega_f$.

source.place: Statement, symmetric projection comparison; same base-change argument with the factors interchanged

proof.text: The closed section from Step 1 has section invariant $C(p_1,\Delta)=L\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}$ by [def-pur-section-invariant]. Apply the functor $L\Delta^*$ to the inverse $b_1^{-1}$ constructed in Step 2. A functor takes an isomorphism and its inverse to mutually inverse maps, since it preserves compositions and identities. This gives the specified isomorphism $C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}L\Delta^*Lp_2^*\omega_f$.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: pull the first projection comparison back along the diagonal

proof.text: Work at $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ as required by [def-pur-conventions]. Apply [lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition] to $h=\Delta:X\to W$ and $k=p_2:W\to X$. Its equality says that the specified coefficient map for $p_2\Delta$ is the composite coefficient map. Thus the ring-sheaf identifications required in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] are the canonical constant-$A$ identifications for these three morphisms, rather than an independently chosen structure map.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), as stated by the cited pro-etale composition node; blueprint item Proof, last sentence, $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] for $h=\Delta$, $k=p_2$ and the compatible constant ring sheaves from Step 5. The finite-level functors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] are these module pullbacks. Invert the canonical comparison and use $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$ from Step 1 to obtain $L\Delta^*Lp_2^*\omega_f\cong L(\operatorname{id}_X)^*\omega_f$.

source.place: Tag 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), as stated by the cited pro-etale composition node; blueprint item Proof, last sentence, $p_2\Delta=\operatorname{id}_X$

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-proetale-derived-pullback-identity] with $X$ and the finite ring $A$ to obtain $L(\operatorname{id}_X)^*\omega_f\cong\omega_f$. Compose this with Steps 4 and 6 to obtain the asserted $C(p_1,\Delta)\cong\omega_f$. Its factors are the specified base-change comparison and the canonical composition and identity comparisons. This proves the finite-coefficient assertion of the fixed purity conventions; higher coefficient versions remain the transports specified there.
